raw_response:
Alright, let me think this through. I've been doing this 30 years, so I know my land.

I have 12 mu. My main system is wheat-maize double crop — that's what most of us around here do. I'll put 9 mu in the wheat-maize rotation, same fields back to back. The other 3 mu I'll put in cotton — prices have been okay and I have that sandier plot that does better with cotton than grain.

**Wheat (9 mu, winter):** I plant in early October after the maize comes off. I use improved varieties like Jimai or Shinong — the seed dealer in town stocks them and my neighbor Old Wang got 500+ kg last year using these. Base fertilizer I put down compound fertilizer (15-15-15) at about 50 kg per mu before planting — that gives me roughly 7.5 kg N, 7.5 P, 7.5 K. Then topdress urea at jointing, about 20 kg urea per mu (~9 kg N). Total N around 16-17 kg/mu. I irrigate 3 times — before winter, at jointing, and at grain filling. Spray 2 times for aphids and powdery mildew. Rotary tillage, that's what I have the machine service for. I aim for 480 kg/mu, hoping for 500.

**Maize (9 mu, summer):** After wheat harvest in June, straight into maize — no-till planting to save time, the summer is short. Hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 or similar — everyone plants these. Compound fertilizer 40 kg as base (~6 kg N, 6 P, 6 K), then urea topdress at big flare stage about 25 kg/mu (~11-12 kg N). Total N 17-18. Irrigate twice — after planting if no rain, and at tasseling. Spray once or twice for borer and armyworm. Target 550 kg/mu.

**Cotton (3 mu, spring):** Plant in late April. I use improved Bt cotton seed — saves a lot on bollworm spray. Base fertilizer heavier, compound 40 kg plus some urea, total N about 15 kg/mu, P 8, K 10 — cotton needs potassium. Plough this field, need deeper work for cotton. Irrigate 3 times from well. Still need to spray 5-6 times — aphids, mites, late-season bollworm. Target 280 kg/mu seed cotton.

I don't want to skimp on fertilizer — a bad harvest costs more than the extra bag of urea.
